newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries in London up in cautious market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries in London up in cautious market.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly higher on Friday, but traders said the upside was limited ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and two- and five-year T-note auctions.

"The market feels distinctively different from the last couple of days when there was much better buying," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "Today it feels the reverse. The market probably has more downside, with the FOMC and the two- and five-year auctions to come next week."
The long bond was at 96-12, to yield 7.04 percent by 1019 GMT, compared with 96-09 in Tokyo and 96-10 in New York.
Traders said Treasuries had weakend overnight after strong housing starts and weekly jobs data but the market was better bid in London.
"The market is under a lot of pressure in the five- and 10-year sectors. There's buying in the five-year sector and a lot of paper for sale in the 10-year sector," the trader said.
At 1019 GMT, 10-year T-notes were at 101-01, compared with 101-03 in Tokyo and 101-01 in New York, while five-year T-notes were at 99-13, down 1/32 from Tokyo and New York.
With no economic data from the U.S. to provide a focus for the market on Friday, analysts said there would be little movement in Treasuries and players would look towards events next week.

"The market will be dominated by speculation on what the Fed will do, but with no information to go on we'll be stuck in very narrow ranges," said Stuart Thomson, chief international economist at Nikko Euorpe in London.
The FOMC will meet on September 24 and traders said the market was fairly evenly split on whether or not the Fed would raise interest rates.
The U.S. Treasury will auction $18.25 billion of two-year notes on Wednesday and $12.50 billion of five-year notes on Thursday.
Two-year T-notes were at 99-23, down from 99-24 in Tokyo and New York.
December T-bond futures were at 107-23 in automated trade, up 2/32 from Thursday's Chicago settlement.
